Marchant strode out in fine style, however, and soon caught his man and carried on to give us yet another win. In the Field Events, Charlie Melchior gained us first place in the Javelin with George Powell second, and A.

Charlie Melchior once again obliged in the Javelin, and moreover is very consistent with his throwing. Our Field Events captain, Charlie Jones, showed an improvement in his long jumping by gaining second place in that event, being beaten by the Police Champion.
In the Field Events our big Irish Guardsman, Pat Ridge, won both the Weight and Discus with very creditable efforts. Charlie Melchior " obliged " once more in the Javelin Throw, and E.
Charlie Melchior and Ron Jeal finished first and second in the Javelin event, and the former has been throwing in consistent style throughout the season.
Watts won the 440 Yards for us, while Charlie Melchior threw 169 ft. 10 ins. to win the Javelin Throw.
Charlie Melchior has again been our outstanding javelin thrower. His best efforts have been 177ft. 5ins. at Imber Court against the Police and 169ft. 10ins. against the N.F.S. at Chiswick.

In the coming season it is hoped to have the help of most of the "boys" who did so well last season, including genial Pat Ridge for the Shot and Discus, Charlie Melchior, evergreen George Powell, and L.
Charlie Melchior and George Powell have again been the backbone of the Club with their Javelin performances allied to their participation in the Shot Putt and Discus.
Eddie Pack was Southern and Inter-Counties 440 yards Champion, and runner-up in the A.A.A. title. Charlie Melchior was second in the Southern and third in the A.A.A.

This loss meant that the brunt of the Shot event fell upon Charlie Melchior. He has gained us useful points in all matches and did a personal best of 34 ft. 8 ins. in the match against the Police at Imber Court.
Charlie Melchior again, and Alan Dunn, one of our most promising younger members, were our mainstays in the Javelin, gaining maximum points in a number of matches.

Charlie Melchior was second in the Javelin Throw, and our field event Captain, Charlie Jones, was second in the Long Jump. Final points were: Belgrave Harriers 68, Metropolitan Police 60, Cambridge Harriers 48.

In the field events, our representatives had very little opposition, and with Charlie Melchior and Syd Jones, we gained maximum points in the Weight and Javelin events.
Charlie Melchior won the Javelin Throw and also gained third place in the Weight Putt. Charlie Jones won the Long Jump and is showing a big improvement in his jumping.

Alan Dunn beat Charlie Melchior in the Javelin Throw in finishing second to Dalyrymple of L.A.C. Final match scores were : Belgrave H. 74, London A.C. 69, Polytechnic H. 65, and we can be well satisfied with our lads' performances against such strong opposition.
Javelin.—1 C.
McKenzie was second for us in the High Jump, thus showing his versatility, Charlie Melchior won the Javelin, and Bill Sutton had a couple of second places in the Weight and Discus.
Weight.—1 C.

Our Javelin throwers, Charlie Melchior, Alan Dunn and veteran George Powell have not shown performances up to their best, but Charlie again won the Hertfordshire County Championship and the Club Championship with a throw of 154 feet 3 inches.
George Lucas lost a close race by inches in the Kent County 3 miles race in record time, and Charlie Melchior won the Javelin Throw in the Hertfordshire event.

Charlie Melchior and George Powell. However, it is to Alan Dunn, Geoff Jarvis, Arthur Allen and Terry Bateman we look for improved performances and from at least one, distances approaching, even if not beating those achieved by the old stalwarts in previous years.

In the Javelin we shall no doubt see our old stalwart George Powell performing again and also Charlie Melchior. If Alan Dunn is now fully recovered from his arm injury he should be our first string backed up by Bateman, Higgins and Bergvalds.
Bergvalds, our Latvian member, scored points for us in the Weight Put and Discus Throw, but we missed the help of Charlie Melchior in the Javelin Throw.
Bergvalds retained his Weight and Discus titles and Charlie Melchior once again won the Javelin Throw.

Charlie Melchior again won the championship, which shows the paucity of good performers. Terry Bateman will, we hope, show considerable improvement, and with Doug Whitehead, now back in “civvy street” aftr getting a R.A.F.
